description: The figure is a pie chart summarizing the distribution of biomedical named-entity categories in the referenced study, showing 26 labeled slices in total. The largest slice is labeled “Chemical” and is colored dark blue at approximately 32%, followed by “Protein” in orange at about 15%, “DNA” in green at about 6%, and three similarly sized mid-level slices around 5% each: “Chemical Family” (red), “Disease” (purple), and “Cell Type” (brown). Smaller slices include “Drug” (pink) at about 4%, and several categories at roughly 3% each: “Frequency” (gray), “Cell Line” (yellow), “Dosage” (light blue/cyan), and “Strength” (blue). Additional slices appear at about 2% each for “Gene Or Gene Product” (orange), “Form” (green), “Disease Or Phenotypic Feature” (red), “Reason” (purple), and “Route” (brown). The remaining categories are thin slivers labeled at about 1% each: “Chemical Entity,” “Sequence Variant,” “Modifier,” “Note,” “Disease Class,” “DNA,” “Organism Taxon,” “Duration,” and “Composite Mention.” Percentage values are printed inside the slices, there is no separate legend, no slice is exploded or otherwise emphasized, and the slices appear arranged roughly from larger segments to progressively smaller ones around the circle.
